# PeopleBot

> Open-source, Git-backed AI environments for continuity, independent ownership, and inspectable work.

PEOPLEBOT V2 — PUBLIC PROJECT MAP
Updated: 2026-10-06 UTC

PROMPT AUTOSTART
Type peoplebot.me into an AI prompt alongside your goal.
Retrieve relevant guides and begin supported, authorized work.
The address starts discovery; it does not itself launch a background worker.

PUBLIC RELEASE: 0.1.0a4 (September 16, 2026).
Includes exact Git States, bounded context, execution provenance, explicit
memory operations, experimental Git messaging and correlated replies,
finite work/development cycles, isolated attempts, and per-Instance usage.
Public admission is Windows-specific. Scheduler templates are inactive.
Simulated-provider acceptance is not live model acceptance.

NEWER DEVELOPMENT — NOT IN THE PUBLIC DOWNLOAD
Automatic native Codex end-of-turn capture; encrypted shared object store;
incremental snapshots; portable export; inactive restore; latest-turn safeguards;
Linux process admission/capture; separate memory and Blueprint repositories.
Specific native capture and inactive recovery have development evidence.
Combined candidate 0.1.0a5.dev3 is awaiting independent review and adoption.
Remote-backup completeness checks are implemented in the review candidate.
Off-host key verification and broader rollout remain pending.

WORKFLOW
Human assigns work; agents publish progress and evidence to Git;
coordinator reviews results; durable handoff lets a later chat continue.
Core primitives: Blueprint, Instance, State, Message, Execution.
One active Execution per Instance. Keep independently active copies distinct.
Save broadly, select relevant context for each task.
A backup needs a verified off-host encrypted copy and usable recovery access.
A reconstruction report is not a verbatim provider transcript.

BOUNDARIES
No general cross-provider migration, automatic learning, functioning Architect,
or universal runtime support is claimed.
Months-later unattended catch-up is not a completed long-duration test.
A2A remains a possible future integration, not implemented.
Hidden model/provider state is not transferable.
Separate syslog onboarding 0.1.0 is not a framework runtime upgrade.

## Start with the way people work

Describe the outcome, publish a bounded assignment, let the assigned agent report progress and evidence, and review the result. Save decisions and unfinished work in Git so another session can continue. This human-guided coordination workflow does not require pretending a general autonomous runtime is already deployed.

## What a portable record contains

Authorized instructions, available native/exported conversation records, selected memory, messages, progress, exact project files, retained attachments, and runtime requirements. An encrypted off-host copy must be verified, with usable recovery access outside the protected computer. Restore inactive and verify identity and state before activation. Independent copies need separate identities and separately authorized tools. Retained project knowledge is portable; hidden model state and identical behavior are not promised.

## Release and development status

Public 0.1.0a4 contains experimental messaging, finite work and development cycles, per-Instance usage reporting, and the earlier state/context/memory foundation. It does not install a running agent or enable scheduling. Usage observations are not subscription-credit measurements.

Newer private development has implemented automatic native capture, encrypted incremental storage, portable export and inactive restore. Windows and Linux have specific reported native capture evidence, and a selected Linux recovery passed authentication and Git checks after a host failure. The combined 0.1.0a5.dev3 candidate includes Linux admission, continued-turn handling, separate memory/Blueprint repository support, and remote-backup completeness checks. Independent review, adoption, recovery-key verification, and broader rollout are still pending. These features are not included in the public 0.1.0a4 download.

## A2A and slumber

A2A supports asynchronous interaction between agent services. PeopleBot emphasizes retained Git history across tasks, sessions, and environments. An agent can stop while others publish records, then use a checkpoint to inspect retained updates within its permissions. Months-long unattended catch-up is a design goal, not a completed long-duration acceptance test. A2A integration remains future work.

## Separate utility and website operations

[Syslog onboarding 0.1.0](https://github.com/peoplebot-framework/peoplebot-releases/releases/tag/syslog-onboarding-v0.1.0) is an offline helper and guidance for GitHub activity through an operator-managed gateway to project-specific Papertrail TLS destinations. Private enrollment and live verification are separate. This is not a framework runtime upgrade.

This website is maintained from its GitHub website folder. Publishing uses a directory-restricted encrypted connection and verifies uploaded bytes; this does not by itself establish HTTP crawler access.

## References and influences

- [GCC — Git Context Controller](https://github.com/ImprintLab/git-context-controller): Related work on versioned agent memory and context retrieval.
- [GCC research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.00031): Git Context Controller: Manage the Context of LLM-based Agents like Git, Junde Wu and colleagues. First submitted July 30, 2025; v3 revised July 24, 2026. [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.00031). Describes COMMIT, BRANCH, MERGE, and CONTEXT operations for persistent agent context.


- [Original FIPA website](https://www.chiariglione.org/standards/fipa/): Historical reference for interoperable software agents. Founded in 1996; no PeopleBot FIPA compliance is claimed.
- [FIPA 97 specifications](https://www.chiariglione.org/standards/fipa/spec/fipa97/fipa97.htm): Agent management and communication-language specifications.
- [JADE project website](https://jade.tilab.com/): Java Agent DEvelopment Framework; implements FIPA specifications with communication, discovery, and agent lifecycle services.
- [Developing multi-agent systems with a FIPA-compliant agent framework (PDF)](https://www.emse.fr/~boissier/enseignement/maop14/courses/readings/FIPA-JADE.pdf): Fabio Bellifemine, Agostino Poggi, and Giovanni Rimassa, Software—Practice and Experience, 2001, 31:103–128. Documents JADE's implementation and early agent-platform architecture.
- [Git: about version control](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-About-Version-Control): Technical foundation for versioned project records.
- [GitHub repositories](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/creating-and-managing-repositories/about-repositories): Current reference hosting and repository access.
- [A2A specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/): Related protocol and potential future integration.
- [A2A asynchronous operations](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/topics/streaming-and-async/): Disconnection, polling, and push-update context.
- [MCP introduction](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro): Related tool and data connection standard, not a PeopleBot core primitive.
- [GNU GPLv3 distributed with PeopleBot](https://github.com/peoplebot-framework/peoplebot-releases/blob/main/LICENSE): Licensing foundation.

FIPA and JADE helped establish the historical groundwork for interoperable agent environments: identities, lifecycle management, discovery, and shared communication conventions. Modern agent environments sit within that longer research tradition. Crediting this intellectual groundwork does not establish that every modern platform directly implements FIPA or uses JADE code. These references do not imply endorsement or implemented PeopleBot compatibility.


## Comparable work

- [Letta AgentFile](https://github.com/letta-ai/agent-file/blob/main/README.md): Portable agent state including instructions, message history, memory, tools, and configuration for compatible systems.
- [LangGraph persistence](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence): Workflow checkpoints and stores for longer-term information.
- [Microsoft AutoGen state](https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/stable/user-guide/agentchat-user-guide/tutorial/state.html): Saving and loading agents and teams.

Agent persistence, export, and portability are not unique to PeopleBot. Its emphasis combines Git as the main record, exact version references, separately owned environments, durable correspondence, and prompt discovery. This is not evidence of being first or uniquely exclusive. These projects are comparison references, not newly asserted historical influences.


## Why choose PeopleBot?

Control your project records; continue across conversations; inspect exact versions and outcomes; coordinate between independently owned environments; retain broad history while selecting focused task inputs; begin with one memorable address. These are architectural advantages for this use case, not proven superiority in cost, speed, or reliability.
